title: LLM prefetch & routing parking lot - Maya Singh
content:
Context and intent:
- Quick personal scratchpad to capture product ideas and tradeoffs for a combined KV-prefetch + routing feature aimed at reducing token costs and tail latency for common LLM app patterns.
- This is a parking-lot / rough PRD outline; goal is to unstick decisions, surface open questions, and propose first experiments.

Problem statement:
- Many customer workloads have stable prefixes (system prompts, few-shot examples, repeated instruction frames) that are repeatedly re-encoded into the KV cache.
- Prefetching/populating KV cache for common prefixes + smart routing to warmed replicas could reduce average latency and per-token compute.
- Risk: increased memory footprint, complexity in eviction, possible quality regressions if stale cached state used incorrectly.

High-level idea:
1) KV-prefetch store: maintain lightweight store of precomputed KV cache blobs keyed by canonical prompt fingerprint (hash).
2) Warmed routing policy: route incoming requests with matching prefix fingerprint preferentially to GPU workers that have the prefetch loaded (warmed pool).
3) Soft-fallback: if warmed capacity is saturated, fallback to normal routing (no blocking).
4) TTL + refresh policies: short TTLs for dynamic contexts, longer for stable system prompts.

Goals / success metrics (initial):
- Latency: reduce median and 95th percentile response time for matched requests by >= 20%
- Cost: reduce average GPU token compute for matched requests by >= 15%
- Accuracy: no meaningful quality regression on eval suite (delta < 0.5% on key metrics)
- Operational: maintain <5% increase in memory footprint per worker in warmed configuration

Target user stories:
- As an app developer, I want my common system prompt + examples to be served faster (lower latency) when requests contain the same prefix so my chat UI feels snappier.
- As an SRE, I want the warmed routing to be transparent and fall back automatically so we never block requests waiting for warmed capacity.
- As a product owner, I want to measure cost savings and user-facing latency to justify enabling warmed routing for paid tiers.

Rough technical approach / components:
- Prefix fingerprinting: normalized tokenization + stable hash (configurable n-gram or full-prefix)
- Prefetch store: metadata + pointer to serialized KV cache blob (S3 or local on node persistent store). Small format: compressed float16 tensors or quantized cache.
- Worker hook: on warm load, worker loads KV blob into KV cache slot; requires a lightweight API to pin/unpin slots.
- Router: extend smart-router to evaluate fingerprint and target warmed pool; maintain warmed pool capacity per model/variant.
- Eviction/TTL: LRU with TTL; configurable per-customer or per-route policy.
- Metrics: histogram of matched vs unmatched latencies, memory increase, load on prefetch store.

Experiments / rollout plan (MVP):
- Phase 0: offline simulation. Run traces over production logs (anonymized) to find high-frequency prefix candidates and estimate potential cache-hit rates.
- Phase 1: read-only warm routing (no writebacks). Implement router logic and pre-warm blobs on a small set of workers; measure latency on shadow traffic.
- Phase 2: controlled canary for a small subset of customers (opt-in). Track quality metrics and cost.
- Phase 3: gradual expansion with auto-scaling warmed pool, publish SDK opt-in flag.

Open questions / risks:
- How to safely fingerprint prefixes that include user-specific tokens (PII)? Need canonicalization rules + opt-out for routes with sensitive data.
- Memory vs throughput tradeoff: how many KV slots per worker before throughput suffers? Need microbenchmarks.
- Model variants: can prefetch blobs be reused across quantized variants? Probably only within compatible kernel/quantization settings.
- Consistency: sequence length and positional embedding offset issues if cached prefix length mismatches live request. Must store metadata with cache indicating starting step/offset.
- Billing: should warmed routing be a paid feature (Dedication) or free for hosted? Pricing discussion needed.

Immediate next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Run offline frequency analysis on last 2 weeks of request traces (ask SRE for agg logs) (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Prototype fingerprinting & prefab KV serializer (owner: Jordan)
- [ ] Spike: router changes to prefer warmed workers (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Write initial test plan + eval prompts to catch quality regressions (owner: Aisha)

References / links:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/kv-prefetch-proposal
- Jira ticket (parking): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RWD-987
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/456
- Slack thread: #kv-prefetch-wg (link: slack://channel?id=kv-prefetch-wg)

Notes to self:
- Keep the first experiment read-only and non-blocking; warmed routing should always have a deterministic fallback.
- Consider offering per-route TTL configuration in Console as an "advanced" setting.
- Explore combining with prefetch fingerprinting + client-side hints (SDK can surface a stable route id).

End of scratchpad. Will refactor into PRD skeleton once offline traces returned and we have basic numbers.
